questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to create a good dating profile with the right photos
Why many dating app users don't actually go on dates
The history of marriage and dating in Britain
How much money dating apps make from their users
questions.why: Neil says few app users actually go on a date, and they find out the reasons.

questions.q: What experience do Neil and Dan have of dating apps?
options: Both use them regularly to meet new people
Only Dan has used them, and he met his partner
Neither has, but Neil has friends who did
Neil met his wife on one ten years ago
questions.why: Neither has used them, but Neil has friends who have, 'very successfully'.

questions.q: According to Elizabeth Tinnemans, what were the most common reasons for using the app?
options: Curiosity, passing time and entertainment
Finding a husband or wife
Making business contacts
Meeting people while travelling
questions.why: She says the most common motives were curiosity and passing time or entertainment.

questions.q: What does Elizabeth Tinnemans say happens fairly often, especially among millennials?
options: Deleting the app after one day
Paying for extra features
Meeting many people in one week
Swiping through the app with friends
questions.why: She says 'swiping with friends is something that happens fairly often'.

questions.q: Why does Dan mention watching people bungee jumping?
options: It is his favourite hobby at weekends
It shows doing something just out of curiosity
He met his girlfriend there last summer
To show that online dating can be dangerous
questions.why: He went to watch out of curiosity but was never going to do it himself.

questions.q: Was Elizabeth Tinnemans surprised that few users met up?
options: Yes, very surprised
Yes, because the app is popular
She didn't comment
No, it made sense given their reasons
questions.why: She says 'it makes sense because we also looked at why they were using' it.

questions.q: According to Zoe Strimpel, what is making dating unpleasant?
options: Having so much choice
Apps being too expensive
Not enough people using apps
Bad technology
questions.why: She links it to 'the sort of incredible sense of choice'.

questions.q: How does Zoe Strimpel say many app users feel?
options: Excited and hopeful about meeting someone special
Confident and happy with the people they meet
Disappointed, tired of it and aware it can be cold
Worried about their privacy and personal data
questions.why: She says people are disillusioned, jaded and aware relationships are often callous.
